challenge.better_approach: Revert the rider for in-process handlers. That removes the bound 4d597cac9f5d exists for; the floor's ask is the one that legitimately runs long, so the floor names its own wait. Looked; this is it.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a tester run never legitimately exceeds 3600 s. Measured: the longest b0e65 run was 1040.8 s, and the longest tester/run on the home bus 1384 s.
challenge.prior_art: 0bcb816d6e9c added STAGE_BUDGET_S for the ticket's own wait past a stage's reply; this reuses it. The floor-cost ticket (cast only, pending) will cut how many proofs run; it does not change how long one may run.
challenge.real_collision: None. The stage itself already runs off her lock (e4714e460e32), so waiting longer holds no shim lock.

answers.falsifier: Done when a scaled 200 s tester run comes back green through _ask_once, the timeout constrain asks with is ticket.STAGE_BUDGET_S read at call time, and a run past the budget still comes back unrunnable. Wrong intent if the floor should not wait for long proofs at all (that is the floor-cost ticket's question, not this one's).
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator ruled it (ii) from the asker census cast on ticket 4d597cac9f5d (CairnCommons/tickets/4d597cac9f5d-bus-request-s-timeout-bounds-a-synchronous-in-process-handler.json)
answers.how: _ask_tester imports STAGE_BUDGET_S at call time and passes it as the request's timeout in place of the literal 180. A red-first proof stubs the tester on a scratch bus and scales every requested timeout by 0.001, so a 200 s run (0.2 s) is unrunnable on 7ae315843 and green after the fix, while a run past the budget still comes back unrunnable.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (an unrunnable verdict is a record and must not claim a fault for a proof that ran green); Law 1 (one budget, imported, not a second copy); outline 3.3.4.3.
answers.what: constrain's floor waits for the tester's run verb up to the stage's budget (STAGE_BUDGET_S, imported from cairn/machines/ticket/ticket.py), so a tester proof that runs longer than 180 s reads as its own verdict, not as unrunnable, now that bus.request's timeout bounds an in-process handler.

bullets.text: After 4d597cac9f5d bus.request bounds in-process handlers, so constrain's 180 s ask would turn every tester proof over 3 minutes (5 of b0e65's 55, up to 1040.8 s) into unrunnable. It now waits the stage budget. A census of every other asker found none that needs the same change.
